Definition: to stray, i.e. (figuratively) sin (with more or less apology)
BiblicalUsage: Shagag is the sin nobody meant to commit, the straying done in ignorance. The law provides a trespass offering for it, and the priest makes atonement for the soul that sins ignorantly before the LORD. The psalmist knows the pattern from his own life, for before he was afflicted he went astray, but now he has kept God's word.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God made room for sins of ignorance because He knows how easily we stray without meaning to. Affliction taught the psalmist what the offering already said, that even an unintentional sin needs atonement.
